boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Maryville University of Saint Louis
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food and convenience stops with publicly posted late hours near Maryville’s Town and Country campus.

cards.title: McDonald's on Clarkson Road
cards.subtitle: Chesterfield, Missouri
cards.notes: Use the restaurant locator before leaving; this Clarkson Road location lists both lobby and drive-thru service around the clock.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour restaurant option in Chesterfield.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's lists its 1701 Clarkson Rd location as open 24 hours daily for both restaurant/lobby and drive-thru service.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists restaurant/lobby and drive-thru open 24 hours Monday–Sunday.

cards.entity_name: The Market at Hyatt Place St. Louis/Chesterfield
cards.title: The Market at Hyatt Place
cards.subtitle: 333 Chesterfield Center, Chesterfield
cards.notes: Check the hotel dining page and enter through the hotel’s public areas; the Market is listed for packaged grab-and-go items.
cards.short_summary: A hotel grab-and-go market with 24-hour posted access.
cards.evidence_claim: Hyatt lists The Market at Hyatt Place St. Louis/Chesterfield as open 24 hours and offering packaged grab-and-go items.
cards.access_notes: Hyatt’s dining page lists The Market as open 24 hours.

cards.title: QuikTrip on Manchester Road
cards.subtitle: 14800 Manchester Rd, Ballwin
cards.notes: Use the store’s posted hours for a late convenience stop; note that its made-to-order kitchen closes earlier than the store.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store on Manchester Road.
cards.evidence_claim: QuikTrip lists Store #621 at 14800 Manchester Rd as open 24 hours every day; its kitchen has separate, earlier hours.
cards.access_notes: Official locator lists the store open 24 hours daily; verify kitchen availability separately.

cards.title: Culver's on Chesterfield Airport Road
cards.subtitle: 17349 Chesterfield Airport Rd, Chesterfield
cards.notes: Plan for a drive-thru, curbside, or dine-in visit before midnight; confirm same-day availability through the restaurant’s official page.
cards.short_summary: A midnight-closing Culver’s in Chesterfield.
cards.evidence_claim: Culver's lists its 17349 Chesterfield Airport Road location’s lobby, dine-in, curbside, and drive-thru hours as 10 AM–12 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Culver's of Chesterfield, MO — Chesterfield Airport Rd
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily service until 12 AM.

cards.title: STL Curry Club on Clarkson
cards.subtitle: 1635 Clarkson Rd, Chesterfield
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s contact page before heading over; it posts midnight operating hours but separate earlier online-order cutoffs.
cards.short_summary: An Indian restaurant posting midnight operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: STL Curry Club posts hours until midnight every day at its 1635 Clarkson Rd location.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists operating hours until 12 AM daily; online-order hours may end earlier.

cards.title: Greentrails Corner Cafe
cards.subtitle: 14276 Ladue Rd, Chesterfield
cards.notes: Make this a Saturday-only late option: the ordering page lists a 9:30 PM–midnight Saturday service window and the Chesterfield address.
cards.short_summary: A Saturday midnight option on Ladue Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Greentrails Corner Cafe's official ordering page lists Saturday hours of 9:30 PM–12 AM at 14276 Ladue Road in Chesterfield.
cards.source_title: Greentrails Corner Cafe — Official Online Ordering
cards.access_notes: Official ordering page lists Saturday service from 9:30 PM until 12 AM.

cards.title: Syberg's Chesterfield
cards.subtitle: 17416 Chesterfield Airport Rd, Chesterfield
cards.notes: For a food-focused late stop, arrive before the kitchen cutoff rather than the building’s closing time; the official page distinguishes the two.
cards.short_summary: A restaurant with late posted kitchen hours on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Syberg's lists Chesterfield kitchen service one hour before its closing time; the location closes at midnight Friday and Saturday and 11 PM Sunday–Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Official page says the kitchen closes one hour before closing: 11 PM Friday–Saturday and 10 PM Sunday–Thursday.

cards.title: Smitty's on Clayton Road
cards.subtitle: 14874 Clayton Rd, Chesterfield
cards.notes: Use the posted kitchen schedule, not only the listed business close; Friday kitchen service runs later than the regular weekday schedule.
cards.short_summary: A Clayton Road restaurant with an 11 PM Friday kitchen.
cards.evidence_claim: Smitty's Food & Drink lists Friday kitchen hours from 11 AM–11 PM at 14874 Clayton Road in Chesterfield.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Friday kitchen hours until 11 PM; weekday kitchen hours end at 10 PM.

cards.entity_name: Mike Duffy's Pub & Grill Town & Country
cards.title: Mike Duffy's in Town & Country
cards.subtitle: 1024 Schnucks Woodsmill Plaza, Town and Country
cards.notes: Confirm the kitchen schedule on the restaurant’s page before going; its latest posted kitchen service is Friday and Saturday until 10:30 PM.
cards.short_summary: A nearby restaurant with 10:30 PM weekend kitchen hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Mike Duffy's Town & Country lists Friday and Saturday kitchen hours from 11 AM–10:30 PM.
cards.source_title: Mike Duffy's Pub & Grill Town & Country
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday kitchen hours until 10:30 PM.

cards.title: Westchester STL
cards.subtitle: 127 Chesterfield Towne Center, Chesterfield
cards.notes: For a Friday or Saturday dinner run, use the posted kitchen cutoff: the restaurant is open to 11 PM, with food service ending at 10 PM.
cards.short_summary: A Chesterfield Towne Center restaurant open until 11 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: Westchester STL lists Tuesday–Saturday hours until 11 PM, with its kitchen closing at 10 PM Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Tuesday–Saturday hours until 11 PM; Friday and Saturday kitchen service ends at 10 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten map-listed Maryville destinations with documented student-facing functions, from research and support to campus activities.

cards.title: University Library
cards.subtitle: Library building, campus map location 14
cards.notes: Use the library as a research stop: the official site links its collections, research help, librarian support, archives, and student-success services.
cards.short_summary: A named campus research and support hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s campus map lists the Library at location 14, and the library site offers research help, librarian support, collections, archives, and student services.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s current hours and directions page before planning a visit.

cards.entity_name: Morton J. May Foundation Art Gallery
cards.title: Morton J. May Foundation Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Inside the Library building, campus map location 14
cards.notes: Add the gallery to a library visit; it is a named destination in the same map-listed building as the library and student-support services.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed art gallery within the library building.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists the Morton J. May Foundation Art Gallery at location 14 with the Library.
cards.access_notes: Check university information for gallery availability or event access before visiting.

cards.title: Donius University Center
cards.subtitle: Campus map location 4
cards.notes: Start here when coordinating campus activities: the map places the Center for Student Engagement, atrium, dining option, and M Store in this building.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed building that groups several student-facing destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists Donius University Center at location 4 with the Center for Student Engagement, Donius University Atrium, L J’s & Louie’s, and M Store.
cards.access_notes: Verify department and venue access with Maryville before visiting.

cards.title: Donius University Atrium
cards.subtitle: Inside Donius University Center, campus map location 4
cards.notes: Use the campus map to locate this named atrium inside Donius University Center, alongside student-engagement and dining destinations.
cards.short_summary: A named atrium within Donius University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists the Donius University Atrium at location 4 in Donius University Center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm building access and any event setup before relying on the space.

cards.title: Center for Student Engagement
cards.subtitle: Inside Donius University Center, campus map location 4
cards.notes: Locate this campus engagement office through Donius University Center when looking for university-sponsored student activities and involvement information.
cards.short_summary: The map-listed student-engagement destination in Donius University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists the Center for Student Engagement at location 4 in Donius University Center.
cards.access_notes: Contact the Center for current programming and office-access information.

cards.title: L J’s & Louie’s
cards.subtitle: Inside Donius University Center, campus map location 4
cards.notes: Use the campus map to find this named dining destination in Donius University Center; review current dining information before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed campus dining destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists L J’s & Louie’s at location 4 in Donius University Center.
cards.access_notes: Food and purchases may be required; confirm current dining service details before visiting.

cards.title: Buder Family Student Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus map location 6
cards.notes: Use the map to find this named student commons, positioned with the Public Safety Office for a practical campus-services stop.
cards.short_summary: A named commons paired with a key campus service on the map.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists Buder Family Student Commons and the Public Safety Office at location 6.
cards.access_notes: Use the university’s current public-safety guidance for assistance needs.

cards.title: Charles M. Huttig Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Campus map location 5
cards.notes: Find this named chapel via the official map and check with Maryville before attending a service, event, or reserved gathering.
cards.short_summary: A distinct map-listed chapel on the Maryville campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists Charles M. Huttig Memorial Chapel at location 5.
cards.access_notes: Availability may depend on services, events, or reservations.

cards.title: Esports Performance Center
cards.subtitle: Campus map location 13
cards.notes: Use the official map to locate this named Esports Performance Center, then check Maryville for current team, program, or facility access details.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated, map-listed esports destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists the Esports Performance Center at location 13.
cards.access_notes: Facility access may be limited to authorized programs or scheduled use.

cards.entity_name: John E. and Adaline Simon Athletic Center
cards.title: John E. and Adaline Simon Athletic Center
cards.subtitle: Campus map location 8
cards.notes: Locate the Simon Athletic Center through the official map; it includes the map-listed Fitness Center, so confirm current access requirements first.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed athletic center that includes the Fitness Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s current campus map lists the John E. and Adaline Simon Athletic Center and Fitness Center at location 8.
cards.access_notes: Confirm facility hours, eligibility, and recreation access rules with Maryville.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten distinct Saint Louis places for a no-admission, no-purchase outing; transportation and optional paid experiences are separate.

cards.title: Walk the Zoo grounds
cards.subtitle: Forest Park, Saint Louis
cards.notes: Meet at either entrance and make a route through the animal areas. Skip paid attractions and parking to keep the visit purchase-free.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided animal-viewing outing with free zoo admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Saint Louis Zoo states that admission is free and that no tickets or reservations are needed to visit.
cards.source_title: Saint Louis Zoo Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Open daily; admission is free. Parking and some attractions cost extra, so arrive by another method or use nearby free street parking where lawful.

cards.title: Browse the collection galleries
cards.subtitle: One Fine Arts Drive, Forest Park
cards.notes: Choose a gallery wing, compare a few works, and regroup in the public collection spaces. Ticketed exhibitions are optional.
cards.short_summary: Free daily museum admission for a self-paced art outing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Saint Louis Art Museum states that admission to the museum is free every day.
cards.source_title: Saint Louis Art Museum Hours and Information
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday; closed Monday. Main exhibitions may be ticketed except on Fridays.

cards.title: Explore St. Louis history exhibits
cards.subtitle: 5700 Lindell Boulevard, Forest Park
cards.notes: Use the permanent and rotating galleries as a conversation starter, then pick one object or story each to share afterward.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop focused on the history of St. Louis and Missouri.
cards.evidence_claim: Missouri's official tourism site states that general admission to the Missouri History Museum is free.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are daily 10 a.m.–5 p.m., Thursday until 8 p.m., and Monday closed; check before travel.

cards.title: Work through the science galleries
cards.subtitle: Saint Louis
cards.notes: Set a small challenge such as finding one exhibit in each gallery that prompts a question, then compare your observations.
cards.short_summary: Free entry to the Science Center's general galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The Saint Louis Science Center describes itself as a free-to-enter nonprofit science center.
cards.source_title: Saint Louis Science Center Spring Campaign
cards.access_notes: General entry is free; ticketed experiences such as films or special programs may have separate charges.

cards.title: See the current CAM exhibitions
cards.subtitle: 3750 Washington Boulevard, Grand Center
cards.notes: Walk the galleries at an unhurried pace and use the posted exhibition information to guide a short discussion with friends.
cards.short_summary: Contemporary-art galleries with no entry ticket required.
cards.evidence_claim: CAM states that admission is always free and tickets are not required for entry.
cards.source_title: Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis Accessibility
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Sunday; verify gallery hours before going. Nearly all public programs are also offered free of charge.

cards.title: Follow an outdoor sculpture route
cards.subtitle: 12580 Rott Road, Saint Louis County
cards.notes: Use the park map to build a short outdoor loop, pausing at sculptures without touching or climbing on the artworks.
cards.short_summary: A free, year-round outdoor art-and-walking outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Laumeier states that the park is free and open to the public year-round, except for special events.
cards.source_title: Laumeier Sculpture Park — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 7 a.m. to 30 minutes past sunset. It closes for certain special events; check the visit page first.

cards.title: Take the sculpture audio tour
cards.subtitle: Downtown Saint Louis
cards.notes: Walk the two-block garden and use its audio tour to choose a few sculptures for a photo-free, conversation-led circuit.
cards.short_summary: Free public sculpture garden with self-guided tour material.
cards.evidence_claim: Citygarden states that it is free to the public and offers self-guided and audio tours.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to 10 p.m. Citygarden is free to the public.

cards.title: Explore the six museum galleries
cards.subtitle: Gateway Arch National Park, downtown Saint Louis
cards.notes: Enter the visitor center, pass security, and move through the museum galleries at your own pace; do not book the tram.
cards.short_summary: Free museum galleries beneath the Gateway Arch.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that the museum under the Gateway Arch is always free and requires no tickets.
cards.source_title: Gateway Arch National Park Fees & Passes
cards.access_notes: Museum access is free and ticketless, but all Arch facility visitors pass through security. The Tram Ride to the Top is paid.

cards.title: Tour the Old Courthouse rooms
cards.subtitle: Gateway Arch National Park, 11 North 4th Street
cards.notes: Visit the historic courthouse as a self-guided stop, then talk through one detail that connects law, place, and public history.
cards.short_summary: A no-ticket historic-site visit within Gateway Arch National Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that entrance to the Old Courthouse is free and does not require tickets.
cards.source_title: Gateway Arch National Park Fees & Passes
cards.access_notes: The NPS lists Old Courthouse access as free and ticketless; confirm opening status before visiting.

cards.title: Visit the Pulitzer galleries
cards.subtitle: 3716 Washington Boulevard, Grand Center
cards.notes: See the current exhibition, then spend time in the outdoor campus spaces while they are open. Keep the outing to free-entry areas.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary and historical art in a museum and outdoor campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pulitzer Arts Foundation states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Museum hours are Thursday–Sunday; its outdoor campus is open daily from sunrise to sunset. Entry and adjacent-lot parking are free.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct campus environments documented by Maryville for studying, small-group work, or quiet breaks between classes.

cards.title: Donius University Center/Library Quad
cards.subtitle: Outdoor space between the Donius University Center and Library
cards.notes: Bring a charged device and use the patio seating when weather permits; the university describes trees, hammocks, and open grass here.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor option with patio seating and trees between two campus landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville identifies this grassy field between the Donius University Center and Library as having patio seating and trees.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; account for weather and follow current campus access guidance.

cards.title: Starbucks Coffee
cards.subtitle: University Library
cards.notes: Use the café setting for reading or laptop work, and plan around any purchase you choose to make; Maryville explicitly names it as a study place.
cards.short_summary: A coffee-shop setting inside the University Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s student-experience page describes Starbucks Coffee as a place to study or grab a bite.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Library according to Maryville’s campus map; confirm current café and building hours.

cards.title: Health and Wellness
cards.subtitle: University Library
cards.notes: Choose this library-area option when a quieter setting suits your work; Maryville describes Health and Wellness as a quiet place and notes yoga classes.
cards.short_summary: A quiet library-area setting associated with Health and Wellness.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville describes Health and Wellness in the library as a quiet place and notes that it hosts yoga classes on some days.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside the Library; verify current building access and whether scheduled programming affects the area.

cards.title: Library Upper Floor
cards.subtitle: University Library
cards.notes: Set up here for focused work using the charging ports and varied seating; move to a quiet room when you need a lower-distraction setting.
cards.short_summary: Upper-level library study space with device charging, varied seating, and quiet rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville says the Library Upper Floor is built for study and has seating types, charging ports, and several quiet rooms.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside the University Library; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Library Lower Floor Lounge
cards.subtitle: University Library
cards.notes: Use the plush seating and table space for a small-group session; bring a fully charged device because Maryville notes limited phone-charging options.
cards.short_summary: A lower-library lounge with soft seating and tables for small-group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville identifies the Library Lower Floor Lounge as fairly quiet with plush seating and table space suited to small groups.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside the University Library; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Louies
cards.subtitle: Donius University Center
cards.notes: Use the extensive seating for a small-group session, but check the campus events schedule first because Maryville notes student events may use the area.
cards.short_summary: A Donius University Center seating area suited to small-group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville describes Louies as having extensive seating and being useful for small groups, while advising visitors to check the event schedule.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Maryville’s campus map lists LJ’s & Louie’s in the Donius University Center; check current event use and building access.

cards.title: Center for Student Engagement
cards.subtitle: Design & Visual Art Building
cards.notes: Choose this for collaborative work when conversation is useful; Maryville describes ample seating and resources, while noting that the space can be loud.
cards.short_summary: A social, resource-rich setting for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville describes Student Engagement as a group-study location with plenty of seating and resources, and notes it can be loud.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Maryville’s campus map places the Center for Student Engagement in the Design & Visual Art Building; verify current building access.

cards.title: Donius University Center Main Hall
cards.subtitle: Donius University Center
cards.notes: Meet collaborators at the tables or booths for an indoor session with large windows; select this when an open, shared setting fits the task.
cards.short_summary: An indoor main hall with lunchroom tables, booths, and large windows.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville says the Donius University Center main hall has lunchroom tables, booths, big windows, and wide-open indoor space for group activities.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside the Donius University Center; confirm current building access and event scheduling.

cards.title: Window-Bay-Bench, Reid Hall 2nd Floor
cards.subtitle: Reid Hall
cards.notes: Use the bench during downtime between Reid Hall classes for a quieter, more secluded seat; bring a layer during colder weather as Maryville advises.
cards.short_summary: A secluded second-floor bench for short individual work sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville describes the second-floor Reid Hall window-bay-bench as quiet, fairly secluded, and offering ample bench space.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Inside Reid Hall; verify current building access before planning a session.

cards.title: Art and Design Lobby
cards.subtitle: Design & Visual Art Building
cards.notes: Use the window-side chairs for an individual reading or laptop block; Maryville notes the seating is limited, so have a nearby backup location.
cards.short_summary: A warm lobby nook with window-side chairs for individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville describes the Art and Design Lobby as quiet and warm, with comfortable chairs beside a large window, while noting only two chairs are available.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Places To Relax On Campus
cards.access_notes: Maryville’s campus map lists the Design & Visual Art Building; verify current building access before visiting.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named public destinations on distinct nearby corridors around Maryville’s Town and Country campus.

cards.title: Conway Park loop
cards.subtitle: Conway Road corridor
cards.notes: Walk the one-mile path around the accent pond, then use the benches or picnic area for a low-key outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A City of Creve Coeur park with a one-mile walking loop and pond.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists Conway Park at 12301 Conway Road and describes a one-mile walking path, accent pond, playground, picnic areas, courts, restrooms, and dog park.
cards.access_notes: The city says its parks open at dawn and close at dusk.

cards.title: Millennium Park splash pad
cards.subtitle: Barnes West Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the paved 0.6-mile trail, or plan a warm-weather stop around the seasonal splash pad and playground.
cards.short_summary: A 25-acre park with a walking trail, playground, splash pad, and historic homestead.
cards.evidence_claim: The city identifies Millennium Park at 2 Barnes West Drive and lists its paved walking trail, playground, seasonal splash pad, pavilions, sports fields, and Tappmeyer Homestead.
cards.access_notes: The city says the splash pad opens Memorial Day weekend and closes Labor Day weekend; confirm conditions before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Dr. H. Phillip Venable Memorial Park
cards.title: Venable Park courts and trail
cards.subtitle: Country View Drive corridor
cards.notes: Bring a racket or take the half-mile paved trail; the pavilion and year-round restrooms make this an easy daytime stop.
cards.short_summary: A 7.5-acre park with courts, playgrounds, a paved trail, and picnic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists Venable Memorial Park at 10630 Country View Drive with a half-mile paved trail, three tennis courts, soccer field, two playgrounds, pavilion, grills, and restrooms.
cards.access_notes: The city says its parks open at dawn and close at dusk.

cards.title: Malcolm Terrace nature trails
cards.subtitle: St. Paul Street corridor
cards.notes: Choose a nature trail through the wooded acreage, then pause in Serenity Grove’s shaded seating area and rock creek setting.
cards.short_summary: A wooded city park with trails, a playground, pavilion, and Serenity Grove.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists Malcolm Terrace Park at 11370 St. Paul Street, off South Mosley Road, with 25 wooded acres, 1.5 miles of nature trails, and Serenity Grove.
cards.access_notes: The city says its parks open at dawn and close at dusk.

cards.title: Lake School Park courts
cards.subtitle: Coeur De Ville Road corridor
cards.notes: Head to the lighted courts for tennis or pickleball, and check the city notice first for any active playground or restroom work.
cards.short_summary: A six-acre park with soccer and lighted tennis courts, including pickleball striping.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists Lake School Park at 581 Coeur De Ville Road with a soccer field and three lighted tennis courts; the first court has pickleball striping.
cards.access_notes: The city notes current construction and restroom information on its parks page; review it before going.

cards.title: LaVerne Collins Park gazebo
cards.subtitle: Old Olive Street Road corridor
cards.notes: Take a book or packed lunch to the gazebo and flagpole monument; this compact park is designed for a quieter stop.
cards.short_summary: A small Creve Coeur park with a gazebo and flagpole monument.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists LaVerne Collins Park at 10581 Old Olive Street Road, at Spoede Road and Olive Boulevard, and identifies its gazebo and flagpole monument.
cards.access_notes: The city says its parks open at dawn and close at dusk.

cards.title: Thornhill’s study rooms
cards.subtitle: Willowyck Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the public computers, Wi-Fi, or study rooms, and browse the branch’s Asian-language collection while you are there.
cards.short_summary: A St. Louis County Library branch with study rooms, Wi-Fi, and an Asian collection.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Louis County Library lists Thornhill Branch at 12863 Willowyck Drive with study rooms, public computers, Wi-Fi, and an Asian collection.
cards.source_title: Thornhill Branch | St. Louis County Library
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8 p.m., Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: Creve Coeur Park Lake
cards.subtitle: Marine Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Follow Dorsett Road west and Marine Avenue north to the lake; plan nature viewing within the listed conservation-area hours.
cards.short_summary: A 320-acre lake area reached from the Dorsett Road and Marine Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Missouri Department of Conservation identifies Creve Coeur Park Lake as a 320-acre area and gives directions via Dorsett Road west and Marine Avenue north.
cards.source_title: Creve Coeur Park Lake | Missouri Department of Conservation
cards.access_notes: Missouri Department of Conservation lists area hours as 8 a.m. to one-half hour after sunset.

cards.title: Longview Farm Park trails
cards.subtitle: Clayton Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the trails and look for the farm house, playground, fountain lake, and Profile Canto VI sculpture during a daytime visit.
cards.short_summary: A 30-acre Town and Country park with trails, historic farm features, and a lake.
cards.evidence_claim: Town and Country lists Longview Farm Park at 13525 Clayton Road and identifies it as a free year-round park; its city material describes trails, the farm house, playground, and fishing lake.
cards.source_title: Parks & Recreation | City of Town and Country
cards.access_notes: The City of Town and Country says its parks are free to visit year-round from sunrise to sunset.

cards.title: Preservation Park trail
cards.subtitle: North Outer Forty Road corridor
cards.notes: Walk the multi-use asphalt trail, then use the playground, volleyball court, or picnic pavilion for an outdoor meet-up.
cards.short_summary: A 12-acre Town and Country park with a trail, playground, pavilion, and volleyball court.
cards.evidence_claim: Town and Country lists Preservation Park at 12625 North Outer Forty Road and describes its picnic pavilion, playground, restrooms, sand volleyball court, and multi-use asphalt trail.
cards.source_title: Preservation Park | City of Town and Country
cards.access_notes: The City of Town and Country says its parks are free to visit year-round from sunrise to sunset.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Maryville traditions, including current campus events and clearly labeled historical practices.

cards.title: Maryville Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide Saints celebration
cards.notes: Watch Maryville’s Homecoming page for the next schedule, then choose a public activity that fits your visit and participation preferences.
cards.short_summary: A current signature Maryville tradition that brings campus and alumni communities together.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville identifies Homecoming as one of its signature traditions.
cards.access_notes: Event timing and individual activity access vary; consult Maryville’s Homecoming page.

cards.title: Cram Jam
cards.subtitle: Finals-week breakfast and study gathering
cards.notes: During finals, look for the campus announcement and join classmates for the study-focused breakfast gathering when it is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: Maryville’s finals-week gathering pairs studying with breakfast and prizes.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville calls Cram Jam one of its most cherished traditions and describes it as a Finals Week gathering in Gander Dining Hall.
cards.source_title: Cram Jam is Back! — Maryville MPress
cards.access_notes: The cited report anticipated Spring Cram Jam; confirm the current semester’s event details with Student Experience.

cards.title: Ring the Saints Success Bell
cards.subtitle: Student Success, University Library
cards.notes: If you have a milestone to celebrate, contact your Life Coach or visit Student Success to arrange a bell ringing and mark the moment.
cards.short_summary: A bell-ringing ritual for students’ academic and personal milestones.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Maryville University of Saint Louis, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A documented orientation-weekend sequence that moves from arrival and connection to campus activities, dining, service, athletics, and a Sunday reset.

cards.title: 1. Start with New Student Move-In Day
cards.subtitle: Campus arrival and residence-hall check-in
cards.notes: Use your assigned arrival time, then settle in and keep the rest of the day flexible for campus orientation activities.
cards.short_summary: The opening stop is Maryville’s scheduled new-student arrival process.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s new-student orientation page lists New Student Move-In Day and says students receive an assigned move-in day and appointment time.
cards.access_notes: For incoming students; follow the university’s assigned move-in instructions.

cards.title: 2. Meet campus at the Resource Fair
cards.subtitle: Friday orientation programming
cards.notes: Make a quick loop through the fair, introduce yourself to one campus resource, and save the contacts you may need later.
cards.short_summary: A structured early-weekend chance to learn services and meet people.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s first-year orientation schedule includes a Friday Resource Fair & Community Meet & Greet.
cards.access_notes: Orientation programming for new students; check the orientation app or university updates for the current schedule.

cards.title: 3. Join My First Friday
cards.subtitle: Friday evening orientation event
cards.notes: Bring a new hallmate or classmate, participate at your own pace, and use the event as a low-pressure introduction to campus life.
cards.short_summary: Friday evening programming gives the weekend a social starting point.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s first-year orientation schedule lists a My First Friday Event on Friday evening.
cards.access_notes: Orientation event; confirm time and location through current university orientation communications.

cards.title: 4. Learn the rhythm at Gander Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus dining stop
cards.notes: Pause for a meal, note the available stations, and ask dining staff about options if you have dietary needs or questions.
cards.short_summary: A campus meal stop that also helps orient you to daily dining routines.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville identifies Gander Dining Hall as a campus dining location with varied menu options and dietary-accommodation contacts.
cards.access_notes: Dining service and payment requirements may apply; consult current dining information before visiting.

cards.title: 5. Catch the Women’s Soccer Game
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning orientation activity
cards.notes: Check the current athletics schedule, arrive with friends, and treat the match as a relaxed way to see campus spirit in action.
cards.short_summary: Orientation programming places an intercollegiate game in the Saturday sequence.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s first-year orientation schedule includes a Women’s Soccer Game on Saturday morning.
cards.access_notes: Game dates, location, and admission conditions vary; verify the current athletics schedule.

cards.title: 6. Step into the M Photo Tradition
cards.subtitle: Saturday orientation tradition
cards.notes: Follow staff directions for the group photo, then keep a copy if one is shared; it makes a simple marker of the start of term.
cards.short_summary: A named, school-specific orientation tradition documented by Maryville.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s first-year orientation schedule explicitly lists the 2026 M Photo Tradition on Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Part of the published 2026 first-year orientation schedule; participation details are set by orientation staff.

cards.entity_name: LEARN. SERVE. LEAD. Community Service Experience
cards.title: 7. Join the community-service experience
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon in St. Louis
cards.notes: Bring what the orientation team requests, work with your CORE 101 peers, and use the return trip to swap notes about the experience.
cards.short_summary: A guided service stop connects new students with the wider St. Louis community.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s orientation schedule lists a LEARN. SERVE. LEAD. Community Service Experience in St. Louis and states transportation will be provided.
cards.access_notes: Published for first-year orientation; transportation and project details are coordinated by Maryville.

cards.entity_name: Men’s Soccer Game & Food Truck Tailgate
cards.title: 8. Return for the Men’s Soccer Game & Food Truck Tailgate
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening orientation activity
cards.notes: Confirm the event details, meet up with your group before kickoff, and choose food based on current vendor availability and payment terms.
cards.short_summary: Saturday evening pairs a soccer game with an orientation tailgate.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s first-year orientation schedule lists a Men’s Soccer Game & Food Truck Tailgate on Saturday evening.
cards.access_notes: Event timing, food vendors, and any payment requirements should be confirmed in current orientation materials.

cards.title: 9. Wind down at Movie on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening outdoor screening
cards.notes: Check the weather and event notice, bring a light layer or blanket if appropriate, and head back with your group afterward.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus screening provides a low-key final Saturday stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s first-year orientation schedule lists Movie on the Quad on Saturday evening.
cards.access_notes: Orientation event; weather plans and start time should be verified through current university communications.

cards.title: 10. Close with the UWOW Kickoff Event
cards.subtitle: Sunday orientation programming
cards.notes: Use the kickoff to identify one club, campus event, or involvement opportunity to explore during your first full week.

cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s first-year orientation schedule lists the UWOW (University Week of Welcome) Kickoff Event on Sunday.
